premises.text: Web data is valuable but currently trapped inside HTML pages
premises.evidence_span: the data's there. It's just trapped. Trapped inside the HTML, the page.

premises.text: The majority of websites do not have an API, making data access complex
premises.evidence_span: the majority of sites do not have an API. And creating one is complex.

premises.text: Import.io allows users to turn any website into a table of data or an API without coding
premises.evidence_span: imagine if you could turn any website into a table of data or an API in a matter of minutes without writing code.

premises.text: Users can create APIs from web pages quickly using the Import.io data browser
premises.evidence_span: I open the Import I.O. data browser, navigate to a web page that has the data on it that I want, and click the I.O. button.

premises.text: Combining created APIs with others is easy and allows for scalable data access
premises.evidence_span: Combining the API that I just created with other APIs is very easy.

premises.text: Import.io has a library of APIs that can be accessed through a Chrome extension
premises.evidence_span: the Data Factory is a Chrome extension that will allow anybody to get access to our library of APIs.

premises.text: The launch of the Data Factory will significantly increase the number of publicly available APIs
premises.evidence_span: In the past 13 years, there have only been 10,000 publicly available APIs created. In the next three months, Import.io will double that number.

value.text: Data on the web becomes easily accessible to everyone
value.evidence_span: for the first time ever, data on the web would be easily accessible to everyone.

notes: User metrics and specific examples of API usage are excluded as traction.
